name: Emeka Lopez

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. This is confidential. What does a normal day at work involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and have managed eight people handling overdue rent on our company’s commercial properties for six years. We match payments to accounts, call tenants before a notice goes out and work out whether a dispute is real or a missed transfer. I have a bachelor’s degree and know the ordinary cases well, though I’m not the best negotiator in the company. I like getting a small shop back on track; I hate the day a notice goes out to someone whose payment we simply filed wrong.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is your household like, and how much space do you have for a pay gap?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife, Nia, is a nurse, and our children are twelve and sixteen. We have a mortgage and less than a month saved, even though we both work; my manager salary is low for this job. There are few offices with this kind of team nearby. I’m cautious with new systems, and I have never used AI, because one wrong rent notice can harm someone’s business.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell my team to check the tenant ledger and call before sending a notice. A small automatic reminder may save time, but it cannot settle a disputed payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My job stays, but the mortgage and our sixteen-year-old’s exam costs still press on us. Nia earns steadily, yet one late bill could swallow what little we have saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I’d keep the morning ledger check and ask the senior clerk to flag payments that do not match a tenant account. In the first year Nia and I would cancel the extra television package and put the 25 a month toward exam fees.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about money, not the software. Keeping my job does not put a spare month in the bank.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you do if a tenant says the payment was sent?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask for the bank reference and search the unmatched payments before sending any letter. A wrongly filed transfer is our error, not a tenant’s character.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why not use a reminder tool yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have never used AI and do not want to learn on a live rent notice. If another manager proves it on old cases, I can listen.

An automatic reminder cannot settle a **disputed transfer**.
think: My **manager job** continues in a plateau.
Exam costs and our **thin reserve** still squeeze the mortgage budget.
do: Keep the **morning ledger check** and flag unmatched payments.
Cancel the **extra television package** to free 25 monthly for exams.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AI will write reminders, match payments and answer tenants, so it must be checked against real disputes. I’d ask management to keep a person accountable for every legal notice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our team may shrink, and eight people might become four. I have experience, but a director could decide one manager is enough for several properties; my own pay would be at risk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I’d ask the finance lead to test thirty closed disputes against the new matching tool, with the senior clerk checking wrong notices. In the first year I’d attend a paid demonstration and learn the tool only if it correctly separates disputed rent from missing payment; I’d ask for written notice before any team merger.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious. A bad match harms a tenant, and a smaller team could leave me looking for scarce local work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would convince you the tool is ready?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d want every unmatched bank reference shown beside the tenant account and the signed lease. A chart of speed is no answer to a false notice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you tell the team your own job might go?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yes. I would say I do not know who remains, and I would show them the result of the test rather than ask for trust.

A **named person** should own each legal notice.
AI will take **routine reminders** and tenant answers first.
think: Our **eight-person team** could shrink to four under this software.
One manager across several properties might cost **my wage**.
do: Ask finance to test **thirty disputes** with the clerk before I use the matching tool.
Learn the tool only after a **paid demonstration** correctly handles disputed rent.
feel: I feel **anxious** about tenants and my own pay.
S1.quote: A chart of speed is no answer to a false notice.
fieldNote: He delegates the first **AI test** and demands signed evidence.
His experience does not guarantee a **manager post** in a smaller team.
He would learn only after **paid proof** on disputed cases.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the company for dates and written severance terms before rent accounts move to a system. Tenants should still be able to speak to someone about a disputed notice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could match, write and negotiate rent better than I do, so I expect my job to end. Nia’s nursing is hands-on and may last until robots arrive around 2031, but her wage alone cannot carry our mortgage and both children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week Nia and I would list the mortgage, exam costs and food and stop the planned holiday deposit. Before 2028 I’d ask her hospital whether paid patient-transport jobs are posted and what shifts they require; in the first year after AGI, I’d apply only if a written wage covers our mortgage share and the shifts leave a parent home at night.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m alarmed. There is less than a month of money behind us. A two-year warning does not make a hospital offer appear.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why patient transport?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It is real hands-on work that the hospital still needs before about 2031 in this picture. I would not call it safe forever, and I would not claim I can do it without training.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the sixteen-year-old about the holiday?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell them we are keeping the mortgage current and their exam costs covered. I would not make them responsible for the job I might lose.

say: I’d demand dates and **written severance terms** before moving rent accounts to software.
Tenants still need a **human dispute contact**.
think: Nia’s hands-on nursing may last until **2031 robots**, but cannot carry the household alone.
do: Stop the **holiday deposit** after reviewing costs with Nia.
Ask about **posted hospital shifts** and apply after 2028 only if written pay covers my mortgage share and night childcare works.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by a thin reserve and short deadline.
S2.quote: A two-year warning does not make a hospital offer appear.
fieldNote: Hospital work is a **temporary bridge** before 2031 robots.
A move needs **written pay and shifts** compatible with parenting.

steps.text: Stop the planned holiday deposit after reviewing mortgage and exam costs with Nia
Ask Nia’s hospital about posted paid patient-transport jobs and shifts before 2028
Apply after 2028 only if written pay covers mortgage share and nighttime childcare works

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say five years gives employers time to show paid vacancies and train people before closing an office. I’d want the hospital to name real shift patterns, not promise work in general.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could try patient transport before my rent job disappears in 2031, if the hospital actually needs staff. The paperwork in a transport lead role would face 2031 AGI too, and the physical work faces robots around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next spring I’d take a paid first-aid course only if the hospital offers it during school hours and Nia agrees to the extra childcare. I’d apply for advertised patient-transport shifts before 2031 only if the written wage covers our mortgage share; in the first year after AGI, I’d stay only while the hospital pays people for hands-on transport.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious but less cornered than in 2028. Five years is enough to ask about shifts without walking away from a paycheck.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the hospital course is unpaid?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not use our small reserve to fund it. I’d ask about a paid route at another nearby service before making a promise at home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Nia want you at the same hospital?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: She would want me to see the actual rota first. We would need one of us at home for the younger child in the evenings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say a decade lets the company name the jobs that really end and the dates they end. Families need time to budget around a wage change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 53 in 2036, with our children older, but the mortgage may remain. I could build an emergency reserve if both wages hold; a different office job would still face the 2036 thinking system, and hospital transport faces robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In January 2027 Nia and I would transfer 75 monthly to savings only after the mortgage and exam costs are paid. I’d stay at the rent office while it pays, ask the hospital each year about posted transport work, and apply before 2036 only if a written wage covers our mortgage share and the shift rota works for both parents; after AGI, I’d stay in transport only while human work is paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious, though a decade gives us room to build a cushion. I’d rather keep one dependable wage while testing the next place.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would stop the savings transfer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A school bill or mortgage rise would stop it for that month. I would not borrow to make a savings target look good.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would another rent office be a safer move?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, it may pay me for a while but still uses the same checking and letters. A new office sign does not protect the work from 2036 AGI.

say: I’d ask the company for a **written list** of jobs that actually end.
Families need **clear dates** to plan around a wage change.
think: The **mortgage** may remain when I am 53.
Another office role faces **2036 AGI**; transport faces 2039 robots.
do: Save **75 monthly** after mortgage and exams; pause for an extra school bill or mortgage rise.

feel: I feel **anxious** but able to build a reserve.
S4.quote: A new office sign does not protect the work from 2036 AGI.
fieldNote: He prioritizes **mortgage and exams** before new saving.
He refuses to call another office a **safe fallback**.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the rent office could close before we have even one month saved. A written severance figure, paid training and an actual hospital rota with wages would help. Nia and I have to know which parent is home at night.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask what a tenant does when a rent notice is wrong and the office has gone. A mistaken notice can shut a small shop before anyone reads its bank reference.

headlineQuote: A mistaken notice can shut a small shop before anyone reads its bank reference.
portrait: **Emeka**, 43, is an experienced rent-collections manager with a bachelor’s degree.
Lower pay and **thin savings** strain a mortgage and two school-age children.
He has **never used AI** and needs proof on disputed rent before learning it.
He considers **hospital transport** only with paid training, written wages and family-compatible shifts.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his rent role before the household builds a one-month reserve.
whatWouldHelp: **Written severance**, paid training and an actual hospital rota with wages would let the family plan.
